name: ADAS (Automated Design of Agentic Systems)
org: University of British Columbia, Vector Institute
one_liner: Meta-agent search evolves Python agent workflows in code space, scoring each candidate on validation data and reporting on held-out test data.

loop.proposes: A meta-LLM writes complete multi-step agent architectures as executable Python forward() functions.
loop.judged_by: An automated benchmark harness executes each candidate workflow on validation tasks (ARC, DROP, GSM8K, MMLU) and computes exact accuracy.
loop.steers: Winning architectures and their validation scores are appended to an growing archive that conditions the next meta-generation step.

headline_result: Discovered agent architectures that outperform hand-designed baselines by up to 13.6 percentage points on ARC logic tasks and transfer across foundation models.
caveat: Evaluated on validation splits of static benchmarks; executing arbitrary LLM-generated code requires sandboxing and incurs high API token cost.
beyond_harness_note: The evolutionary archive loop calls the meta-model to synthesize new workflow programs and retains the discovered code artifacts.
algorithmic_authority: Sandboxed Python execution and validation benchmark evaluator

sources.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems (ICLR 2025 / arXiv:2408.08435)

verification.notes: Checked against Hu et al., arXiv:2408.08435.
